1 --- 2 title: Migrating to Cache Components 3 nav_title: Migrating to Cache Components 4 description: Learn how to migrate from route segment configs to Cache Components in Next.js. 5 related: 6 title: Next Steps 7 description: Learn about other behavior changes when Cache Components is enabled. 8 links: 9 - app/guides/instant-navigation 10 - app/getting-started/caching 11 - app/guides/preserving-ui-state 12 - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components 13 - app/guides/authentication-with-cache-components 14 - app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params 15 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 16 --- 17 18 When [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled, route segment configs like `dynamic`, `revalidate`, and `fetchCache` are replaced by [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 19 20 The migration is driven by **instant navigation validation**. With Cache Components enabled, Next.js validates in development whether navigating into each route renders instantly, and surfaces the code that would block it as an error or insight. 21 22 ## Use the adoption skill (recommended) 23 24 The [`next-cache-components-adoption`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/tree/canary/skills/next-cache-components-adoption) skill drives this migration with a coding agent, one feature at a time, checking in at every feature boundary. It supports two modes: 25 26 - **Incremental.** Opens a single mechanical PR that opts every route out of validation, then ships each feature as a follow-up PR. This automates the [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) flow below. 27 - **Direct.** Adopts every route in place on one branch. 28 29 Install the skill: 30 31 ```bash filename="Terminal" 32 npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption 33 ``` 34 35 Then give the agent this prompt: 36 37 ```prompt 38 Adopt Cache Components in this project using the next-cache-components-adoption skill. 39 ``` 40 41 ## Or migrate by hand 42 43 Migrating an existing app by hand follows a few steps, in order: 44 45 1. [Enable Cache Components](#enable-cache-components) in `next.config.ts`. 46 2. Decide your approach: convert every route now, or [adopt incrementally](#adopting-incrementally) by [opting routes out of validation](#opting-out-of-validation) first and converting one at a time. 47 3. [Follow the validation errors and insights](#following-validation) it surfaces, replacing each route segment config with its Cache Components equivalent and caching uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). The per-key sections below cover each config and API. 48 49 Your existing `fetch` and `unstable_cache` caching keeps working. Migrating `unstable_cache` is optional and can happen later. 50 51 Some surfaces have their own steps: 52 53 - For routes with dynamic params, follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. 54 - For metadata, follow the [`generateMetadata` and `generateViewport`](#generatemetadata-and-generateviewport) guidance. 55 56 The sections below cover each config and API and what to do with it under Cache Components. 57 58 ## Enable Cache Components 59 60 Cache Components requires Next.js 16. If you're on Next.js 15 or earlier, upgrade first by following the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16). Coming from an older version, work through the [upgrade guides](/docs/app/guides/upgrading) to reach 16 before continuing. 61 62 Then enable the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) flag in `next.config.ts`: 63 64 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 65 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 66 67 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 68 cacheComponents: true, 69 } 70 71 export default nextConfig 72 ``` 73 74 > **Good to know:** If you were using `experimental.dynamicIO` or `experimental.useCache`, `cacheComponents` replaces them. See the [version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). 75 76 After enabling the flag, route segments that still export `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache` will error. Start by replacing those configs. The sections below explain what to do for each one. 77 78 ## Opting out of validation 79 80 A validation insight or error tells you a route won't render instantly. Resolve it by following the recommendation: cache the data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrap it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). If you're not ready to address it yet, set the [`instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) config to `false` on the segment that raised it (a layout, page, or parallel slot), then come back to it later. 81 82 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 83 export const instant = false 84 ``` 85 86 > **Good to know**: `instant = false` marks a segment as _allowed to block_. It does not force the route to be dynamic, so a genuinely prerenderable route still ships a static shell. It also does not clear synchronous IO build errors: calls like `new Date()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` still fail the prerender. See [Adopting incrementally](#adopting-incrementally). 87 88 ## Adopting incrementally 89 90 You don't have to migrate every route at once. `instant = false` lets you get the whole app building and running first, then convert routes one at a time: 91 92 1. **Enable the flag and migrate each route segment config.** Follow the relevant sections below for [`dynamic = "force-dynamic"`](#dynamic--force-dynamic), [`dynamic = "force-static"`](#dynamic--force-static), [`dynamic = "error"`](#dynamic--error), [`revalidate`](#revalidate), and [`fetchCache`](#fetchcache). For routes with dynamic params, also follow the [`generateStaticParams`](#generatestaticparams-and-dynamicparams) guidance. Routes that still render instantly need no further work. 93 2. **Opt out the routes that aren't ready.** Where an insight or error appears, set `instant = false` on the segment that raised it. To do this in one pass across the whole app, run the [`cache-components-instant-false`](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#cache-components-instant-false) codemod, which adds the opt-out to every `page`, `layout`, and `default` that doesn't already declare `instant`: 94 95 ```bash filename="Terminal" 96 npx @next/codemod@canary cache-components-instant-false ./app 97 ``` 98 99 > **Good to know**: Pass `./src/app` in a `src/` project. A wrong path reports `0 ok` instead of failing, so check the file count. 100 101 The app keeps building and serving, now with validation deferred for the opted-out routes. 102 103 3. **Fix synchronous IO. It can't be deferred.** Calls like `new Date()`, `Date.now()`, `Math.random()`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` during prerender throw a build error that `instant = false` does not clear, so a route that uses them won't build until you address it, opt-out or not. Move the call out of the prerendered shell so it runs at request time: wrap the part that needs it in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) and call [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) before the call, or move it into a Client Component. 104 4. **Convert one route at a time.** Remove `instant = false` from a route, then resolve its insights by caching data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or wrapping runtime data in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). Repeat until no routes opt out. 105 106 ## Following validation 107 108 Cache Components validates your routes in development and surfaces errors and insights in the dev overlay. Some look like this, naming the affected component and pointing at a fix: 109 110 111 ' }, 119 { text: '}' }, 120 ]} 121 /> 122 ', highlight: true }, 128 { text: ' ' }, 129 { text: '', highlight: true }, 130 ]} 131 /> 132 133 134 Each card is clickable and opens a page with patterns, code samples, and trade-offs. Work through the insights and errors until they're gone. For the full validation workflow, the DevTools, and CI testing, see the [instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation). 135 136 Insights don't show up in the HTTP response. An offending route still returns `200` with rendered HTML in dev. The insight only appears in the dev overlay, the dev-server log, or the [MCP `get_errors` tool](/docs/app/guides/mcp). To see them, read the overlay (or query the MCP). 137 138 ## `dynamic = "force-dynamic"` 139 140 **Remove the config.** Without Cache Components, `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` rendered the entire route for every request and made its `fetch` requests uncached. With Cache Components, uncached data and [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) already run at request time. Next.js prerenders any static or cached UI around them. 141 142 After removing the config, [follow any validation errors or insights](#following-validation) that appear. 143 144 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 145 // Before 146 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 147 148 export default function Page() { 149 return
...
150 } 151 ``` 152 153 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 154 // Before 155 export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' 156 157 export default function Page() { 158 return
...
159 } 160 ``` 161 162 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 163 // After 164 export default function Page() { 165 return
...
166 } 167 ``` 168 169 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 170 // After 171 export default function Page() { 172 return
...
173 } 174 ``` 175 176 ## `dynamic = "force-static"` 177 178 **Remove the config and keep the route fully prerendered.** Without Cache Components, `dynamic = 'force-static'` forced the route to prerender, cached its data, and made `cookies()`, `headers()`, and `useSearchParams()` return empty values. 179 180 Cache uncached data with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and a suitable [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). After removing the config, Request-time APIs read actual request values. Remove those dependencies if the route must remain fully prerendered. 181 182 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 183 // Before 184 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 185 186 export default async function Page() { 187 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 188 return
...
189 } 190 ``` 191 192 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 193 // Before 194 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 195 196 export default async function Page() { 197 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 198 return
...
199 } 200 ``` 201 202 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 203 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 204 205 // After 206 export default async function Page() { 207 'use cache' 208 cacheLife('max') 209 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 210 return
...
211 } 212 ``` 213 214 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 215 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 216 217 // After 218 export default async function Page() { 219 'use cache' 220 cacheLife('max') 221 const data = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 222 return
...
223 } 224 ``` 225 226 ## `dynamic = "error"` 227 228 **Remove the config.** Without Cache Components, `dynamic = 'error'` required the route to prerender and treated `fetch` requests as cached by default. It raised an error only when uncached data or a Request-time API prevented prerendering. 229 230 After removing the config, `fetch` no longer inherits that cached default. To preserve the route's existing caching behavior, wrap those requests in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and set their lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). If the route did not rely on the default, no replacement is needed. 231 232 ## `revalidate` 233 234 **Replace revalidation times greater than zero with `cacheLife`.** Without Cache Components, `revalidate` set the default revalidation time for an entire route. With Cache Components, place [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) around the data or UI that should be cached, then set its lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 235 236 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 237 // Before 238 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 239 240 export default async function Page() { 241 return
...
242 } 243 ``` 244 245 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 246 // Before 247 export const revalidate = 3600 // 1 hour 248 249 export default async function Page() { 250 return
...
251 } 252 ``` 253 254 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 255 // After 256 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 257 258 export default async function Page() { 259 'use cache' 260 cacheLife('hours') 261 return
...
262 } 263 ``` 264 265 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 266 // After 267 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 268 269 export default async function Page() { 270 'use cache' 271 cacheLife('hours') 272 return
...
273 } 274 ``` 275 276 > **Good to know**: If your `revalidate` value doesn't match a built-in [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) profile (`'seconds'`, `'minutes'`, `'hours'`, `'days'`, `'weeks'`, `'max'`), pick the closest one or define a [custom profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#custom-cache-profiles) to match your conventions. You can also [redefine a built-in profile](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#overriding-the-default-cache-profiles), including `default`, when its timings don't match your application's caching needs. 277 278 For `revalidate = 0`, remove the config. Uncached data already runs at request time with Cache Components. Keep data outside a `use cache` scope when it must run for every request. 279 280 ## `fetchCache` 281 282 **Remove the config and set caching at the data source.** Without Cache Components, `fetchCache` changed or restricted the `cache` option for every `fetch` request in a route. With Cache Components, fetches are uncached unless they run inside a `use cache` scope. 283 284 For `default-cache`, `only-cache`, or `force-cache`, wrap the data that should remain cached in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). For `default-no-store`, `only-no-store`, or `force-no-store`, leave the data outside a cache scope. If `force-no-store` previously overrode an explicit cache option, remove that option as well. 285 286 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 287 // Before 288 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 289 ``` 290 291 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 292 // Before 293 export const fetchCache = 'force-cache' 294 ``` 295 296 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 297 // After 298 export default async function Page() { 299 'use cache' 300 // All fetches here are cached 301 return
...
302 } 303 ``` 304 305 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 306 // After 307 export default async function Page() { 308 'use cache' 309 // All fetches here are cached 310 return
...
311 } 312 ``` 313 314 ## `fetch` cache options 315 316 **Move `cache` and `next` options to `use cache`.** 317 318 Without Cache Components, you cache a request with `cache: 'force-cache'` and tune it with `next: { revalidate, tags }`. 319 320 With Cache Components, wrap the fetch in a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) function. Fetches inside that scope are cached automatically, and `revalidate` and `tags` become [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 321 322 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 323 // Before 324 export default async function Page() { 325 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 326 cache: 'force-cache', 327 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 328 }) 329 const data = await res.json() 330 return
...
331 } 332 ``` 333 334 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 335 // Before 336 export default async function Page() { 337 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data', { 338 cache: 'force-cache', 339 next: { revalidate: 3600, tags: ['data'] }, 340 }) 341 const data = await res.json() 342 return
...
343 } 344 ``` 345 346 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 347 // After 348 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 349 350 async function getData() { 351 'use cache' 352 cacheLife('hours') 353 cacheTag('data') 354 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 355 return res.json() 356 } 357 358 export default async function Page() { 359 const data = await getData() 360 return
...
361 } 362 ``` 363 364 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 365 // After 366 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 367 368 async function getData() { 369 'use cache' 370 cacheLife('hours') 371 cacheTag('data') 372 const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data') 373 return res.json() 374 } 375 376 export default async function Page() { 377 const data = await getData() 378 return
...
379 } 380 ``` 381 382 Note the persistence difference. The `fetch` Data Cache persists cached responses across deployments and across serverless instances. 383 384 `use cache` defaults to in-memory storage, so its entries are discarded when the serverless instance is destroyed and are scoped to a single deployment. Use [`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) or a [cache handler](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) for storage that survives instance teardown. Even with durable storage, expect cached values to recompute after a new deployment. 385 386 ## `unstable_cache` 387 388 **No change required.** 389 390 `unstable_cache` continues to work with Cache Components. You can leave it in place and migrate it later. 391 392 If you choose to migrate it, turn the wrapped function into a function with the `'use cache'` directive. The cache key is derived automatically from the arguments, so the key-parts array is no longer needed, and the `options` object maps to [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag). 393 394 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 395 // Before 396 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 397 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 398 399 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 400 async (id: string) => { 401 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 402 }, 403 ['user'], // cache key prefix 404 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 405 ) 406 ``` 407 408 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 409 // Before 410 import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache' 411 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 412 413 export const getUser = unstable_cache( 414 async (id) => { 415 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 416 }, 417 ['user'], // cache key prefix 418 { tags: ['users'], revalidate: 3600 } 419 ) 420 ``` 421 422 ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 423 // After 424 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 425 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 426 427 export async function getUser(id: string) { 428 'use cache' 429 cacheLife('hours') 430 cacheTag('users') 431 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 432 } 433 ``` 434 435 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 436 // After 437 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 438 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 439 440 export async function getUser(id) { 441 'use cache' 442 cacheLife('hours') 443 cacheTag('users') 444 return db.query.users.findFirst({ where: eq(users.id, id) }) 445 } 446 ``` 447 448 Like the `fetch` Data Cache, `unstable_cache` persists cached values across deployments and serverless instances, while `use cache` does not. See [`fetch` cache options](#fetch-cache-options) above for the storage details. 449 450 ## `React.cache` 451 452 **Usually no change.** `React.cache` continues to deduplicate matching calls within a React render. 453 454 However, each Cache Function has an isolated React cache scope. Calls from separate Cache Functions do not share a `React.cache` result, such as when one Cache Function preloads data and another consumes it. 455 456 When a helper reads request data and matching calls need to share work across Cache Function scopes, replace the React wrapper with [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). If the function only needs request-scoped deduplication, use `cacheLife({ stale: Infinity })` so it does not lower the route's stale time. Private Cache Function results are not stored in a server cache across production requests. 457 458 ## On-demand revalidation (`revalidateTag`, `revalidatePath`, `updateTag`) 459 460 On-demand invalidation still works by tagging cached data and expiring it after an event. Tag data with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside a `use cache` function instead of the `fetch` `next.tags` option, then choose the invalidation API by the behavior you want: 461 462 - [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag): for mutations whose result the user must see immediately (read-your-own-writes). Called from a Server Action, it expires the tag so the next request waits for fresh data instead of serving stale content. 463 - [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag): for stale-while-revalidate. A cache profile is **required** as the second argument, for example use `'max'` to serve cached data while it refreshes in the background. 11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
49	
50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55	
56	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
57	
58	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
59	
60	## Version History
61	
62	| Version | Change                                                                                                                            |
63	| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
64	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` introduced. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
